title: (a)/(b) Reaction coefficient: justify 2β − (β+μ) = β − μ and the factor 2 (binary division)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: **Verification obligation, parts (a)-(b).** The zeroth-order term of the expanded integral is $+2\beta(x)F(x)$ (binary division, factor 2), and the loss term is $-(\beta+\mu)F$. The net reaction coefficient is therefore $(\beta-\mu-\lambda)$. The problem writes this as $[2\beta-\beta-\mu-\lambda]$. A proof must show explicitly that (i) the factor $2$ multiplies only the gain integral, (ii) there is no double-counting of $\beta$, and (iii) the zeroth Taylor order of $2\int\varphi g$ is exactly $2\beta F$ (uses $\int\varphi=1$). Small but error-prone; must be written out.
